correctness.rationale: A fully specified finite Bernoulli product space has only six independent effective bonds. The proof explicitly counts all 64 bond sets, separating strong/weak successes and uniform-root component membership. Six nonzero coefficient vectors factor into X=(1-p)(1-g)(p-g)^2 and Y=(1-p)g(p-g)^2, yielding the entire distribution uniformly in all real 0<=g,r<=1. Moments, the one-quarter crossover, full-outbreak tail order and strict aliases follow exactly. The embedded standard-library checker passes 338 rational assertions including an independently enumerated nine-opportunity space of size 512; finite tests are only supplemental.

value.rationale: Four is the first site count admitting two nonisomorphic connected local contact trees, making the comparison natural rather than an arbitrary slice. The all-parameter difference law yields a striking universal reversal of mean risk at global mixing 1/4, disagreement between mean risk and total-outbreak risk, and exact loss of both first and second moment discrimination while the laws differ. The explicit complete classification is a useful finite benchmark for mixed-contact epidemic models; no empirical prediction or large-network generalization is asserted.
